inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 2,114,553,503 shares in issue at 30 Jun 2026 less 3,260,000 treasury shares = 2,111.29m, plus 14.06m dilutive share options/awards per the H1 FY2026 diluted-EPS note = 2,125.4m. Includes the 79.7m shares placed on 27 Jan 2026 (non-SBC issuance, already in the count). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR cash-flow statement line 'Equity-settled share-based payment expenses' (note 9(b)) = RMB(83.079)m, a REVERSAL of unvested awards, not a normal expense year. For the owner-FCF base the deduction uses the FY2021-FY2025 five-year average of the same line (37.1 + 105.3 + 76.4 + 152.0 - 83.1 = 287.8 / 5 = RMB57.6m). No cash taxes on net-share settlement are disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year).
inputs.interest_income_source: FY2025 interest on bank deposits is split across two lines: RMB37.600m in finance income (CF statement 'Interest income from bank deposit') PLUS RMB168.566m inside 'Other operating income' (note 8(a)). Both are earned on the cash pile that is added back in the bridge, so both are stripped (total RMB206.166m). Stripping only the 37.6m finance-income line would count ~RMB170m/yr of the net cash twice.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 share repurchases nil. H1 FY2026 bought 3.32m shares into treasury (immaterial); not a systematic repurchaser, so the flat count is a modelling convention funded by the SBC charge, not by buybacks.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. fx_rate is CNY->HKD = 1.1729 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-22; HKDCNY=X 0.8517 is the reciprocal, 1/0.8517 = 1.1741, a 0.1% tie). Per-share values computed in RMB then multiplied by 1.1729. No dual listing exists for a parity check; cross-check: FY2025 final dividend HK$0.31/share x 2,105m shares = HK$653m = RMB557m, against RMB565.8m dividends paid in the FY2025 CF statement (98% tie, the residual being the interim). Rate must be refreshed with the price; refresh_price.py does not touch it.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 Jun 2026 interim: interest-bearing debt RMB3,863.6m = bank loans 555.4 + 482.2, related-party loans 72.4 + 258.6, medium-term notes 1,495.2 + 499.8, short-term notes 500.0 (no convertible bonds outstanding; lease liabilities RMB273.5m EXCLUDED under lease treatment B). Cash and deposits RMB7,603.3m. Net cash RMB3,739.7m ties exactly to the company's own 'net cash balance of RMB3,739,696,000'. ~47% of the cash sits in the partly-owned subsidiaries Safeway and CLPT (interim p.2225), which is why the NCI is deducted in full at book. The RMB1,000m 1.93% perpetual notes issued 28 Jul 2026 are AFTER the balance date and are excluded from both cash and claims (net nil to common equity; the ~RMB19m/yr coupon is ~RMB0.01/share of leakage, noted, not modelled).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the flows' currency: China 10-year CGB ~1.8%, equity risk premium 7.0% for a HK-listed Chinese cyclical industrial (mature-market 5% plus China country/governance premium), beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~9.5%; after-tax cost of debt ~2.0% (MTN/short-term note coupons 1.6-2.4%); gross debt is ~25% of EV-weighted capital -> blended ~7.6%. Rounded UP to 8.5% because the company is net cash (debt weight overstates the cheap-capital share) and the cash pile earns ~2.7%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, margin risk and segment concentration are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not a second time in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. FY2025 lease cash = principal RMB54.674m (financing, 'Payment of lease liabilities') + interest RMB6.913m = RMB61.6m = 0.23% of revenue, charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path 0.25%. Lease liabilities (RMB226.9m + 46.6m at 30 Jun 2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for the cash-tax EBIT uses the CF-statement 'Depreciation and amortisation' RMB442.4m (1.68% of revenue), which is ex right-of-use depreciation (the 508m 'Depreciation' KPI includes ROU), so the lease is charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at book value RMB1,612.3m (30 Jun 2026 balance sheet). NCI share of FY2025 profit was only RMB36.4m (3.1% of RMB1,171.6m), so the book deduction (11% of total equity) is the conservative side; chosen because ~47% of the group cash pile sits inside the partly-owned Safeway (301559.SZ-listed) and CLPT subsidiaries and the book NCI is the cleanest single claim on it.
inputs.ebitda_definition_note: ebitda_margin_path is UNDERLYING EBITDA: reported EBITDA (post-SBC expense) with the SBC line added back and the RMB168.6m deposit interest sitting in 'other operating income' removed (it is stripped from the FCF base and its asset is in the bridge). FY2025 = (1,988.8 - 83.1 - 168.6) / 26,325.9 = 6.6%; FY2024 = (2,019.0 + 152.0 - 188.5) / 24,755.7 = 8.0%; FY2023 = 8.1%; H1 FY2026 ~6.8%. Government grants (~RMB83m) and the advanced-manufacturing VAT deduction (~RMB33m) are recurring and left in.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company route, non-US cyclical industrial adaptations: CNY-built WACC, lease treatment B, NCI deducted in bridge, full deposit interest stripped, CNY->HKD bridge). Business: LNG/clean-energy equipment and small/mid LNG carrier shipbuilding (78% of revenue), tank containers via listed CIMC Safeway, and European liquid-food process equipment. PRICE: HKEX regular close, not after-hours. FX: 1.1729 CNY->HKD dated 2026-10-22. ANCHORS: price 2026-10-22; net cash, NCI and share count from the 30 Jun 2026 interim (latest filing); flows from FY2025 (31 Dec 2025) with H1 FY2026 used to set FY2026. last_fcf = 807.184 - 57.556 (normalised SBC) - 206.166 (total deposit interest) = 543.462; FY0 owner FCF after the RMB54.7m lease principal that treatment B charges forward is ~RMB489m (1.9% of revenue) -- the capex (3.6%) vs D&A (1.7%) gap on a 6.6% underlying EBITDA margin is why conversion is low, and why the FY2022 10% owner-FCF margin (a working-capital release year) is not carried forward. Horizon 10 years: margins and capex intensity are still normalising in year 5. SBC-light but not SBC-zero: band_position is computed, and the house/street gap is small (~0.3% of revenue).
inputs.guidance_note: No numeric FY2026 guidance (HK-listed industrial practice). FY2026 base growth +3% is set from H1 FY2026 revenue +2.0% (clean energy +8.2%, chemical/environmental +16.0%, liquid food -38.3%) with a recovering liquid-food order book in H2; FY2027-28 at +6% reflects the RMB24.9bn remaining performance obligations at Dec-2025 (0.95x revenue, +16% YoY) and the offshore shipbuilding slate scheduled through 2028.

equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 interim balance sheet line 'Non-controlling interests' RMB1,612,302k; charged once here, flows consolidated (see nci_treatment)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-case 10-year average revenue growth. Equity 5-yr CAGR (10.8%) is the house primary but is backward-looking here: it embeds the FY2021-23 LNG upcycle, retained earnings at a 50% payout, and FY2025 ends before the Jan-2026 placement; H1 FY2026 revenue is +2% with profit -8%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 10.8% diverges 35% from revenue 5-yr CAGR 16.5% (revenue growth has outrun book growth because margins compressed: underlying EBITDA margin 8.4% FY2021 -> 6.6% FY2025). EPS 5-yr 13.6% is within tolerance.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - ALL deposit interest), RMB m: FY2020 543.4, FY2021 -327.1, FY2022 1,971.9, FY2023 685.8, FY2024 963.1, FY2025 543.5 (normalised SBC; 684.1 on the actual -83.1 reversal). Owner-FCF 5-yr CAGR ~0% vs reported 7.1%, and 3-yr -35% vs -27%: the gap is the deposit-interest strip (RMB206m, 26% of reported FY2025 FCF) more than SBC. FCF is too lumpy for a CAGR to be a growth signal -- FY2021 was a working-capital drain, FY2022 a release -- so the revenue path is anchored to backlog and segment trends instead.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +3% from H1 +2% with liquid-food backlog recovering; FY2027-28 +6% on the RMB19.1bn offshore vessel backlog delivering through 2028 and RMB24.9bn group RPO; fades to 2.5% as the LNG newbuild supercycle normalises and hydrogen/ammonia/methanol stay sub-scale.
base.margin_rationale: Underlying EBITDA 6.6% FY2025 / ~6.8% H1 FY2026 recovers only to 7.3% -- below the 8.0-8.1% of FY2023-24 -- as tank-container pricing stays weak and shipyard utilisation improves; no re-rating to the 10% of FY2018.
base.capex_rationale: FY2025 3.6% (shipyard/hydrogen capacity) falls toward 2.5% maintenance as the yard build-out completes; D&A rises from the ex-ROU 1.7% toward 1.9% to meet it.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax on EBIT: FY2023 18.5%, FY2024 17.6%, FY2025 23.2% (tax paid / (EBITDA - D&A)); PRC 25% statutory with 15% high-tech rates at several subsidiaries and overseas mix -> 20% flat.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer/shipbuilder: receivables + inventory partly offset by RMB5.2bn contract liabilities (customer advances). FY2021-25 cumulative cash generated from operations (RMB9.57bn) vs cumulative EBITDA (9.37bn) says working capital is ~neutral over the cycle, but H1 FY2026 swung to a RMB247m operating outflow; -5% of the revenue increase is a modest growth drag.

bull.narrative: Offshore LNG/bunkering vessel backlog converts at improving yard margins, DNV's 198-vessel 2030 bunkering fleet gap keeps order intake above RMB10bn/yr, liquid food recovers on the rebuilt order book, and the coke-oven-gas-to-hydrogen turnkey model replicates overseas; underlying EBITDA margin returns to the FY2023-24 8% level and contract-liability funding keeps working capital near neutral.

bear.narrative: The 2021-25 alternative-fuel newbuild ordering supercycle rolls over (2025 orders already down to 37% of newbuilds from 44%), the IMO Net-Zero Framework delay stalls shipowner fuel-choice capex, Western port-fee/tariff measures on Chinese-built vessels deter European and Singaporean owners, tank-container overcapacity persists and liquid food does not recover; the H1 FY2026 pattern of flat revenue, falling profit and operating cash outflow becomes the run-rate, with underlying EBITDA margin settling at 6%.

scenario_narratives.base: Clean energy (78% of revenue) carries the group: the RMB19.1bn offshore vessel backlog delivers through 2028 and onshore LNG equipment rides record LNG-truck sales, while tank containers and liquid food stabilise rather than recover. Revenue compounds ~4.5%/yr over the decade; the underlying EBITDA margin recovers only to 7.3% from 6.6% as price competition in LNG equipment and tank containers offsets yard utilisation gains; capex intensity falls from 3.6% to 2.5% once the shipyard and hydrogen build-out is done, which is where most of the FCF improvement comes from. Hydrogen, ammonia and green methanol are kept as free options: nothing in the flows depends on them.
scenario_narratives.bull: Offshore LNG/bunkering vessel backlog converts at improving yard margins, the structural bunkering-fleet gap keeps order intake above RMB10bn/yr, liquid food recovers on the rebuilt order book, and the coke-oven-gas-to-hydrogen turnkey model replicates overseas; underlying EBITDA margin returns to the FY2023-24 8% level and contract-liability funding keeps working capital near neutral.
scenario_narratives.bear: The alternative-fuel newbuild supercycle rolls over, IMO delay and Western measures on Chinese-built vessels stall offshore orders, tank-container overcapacity persists and liquid food does not recover; the H1 FY2026 pattern of flat revenue, falling profit and operating cash outflow becomes the run-rate at a 6% underlying EBITDA margin. Net cash means this is a value-erosion path, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: 78% of revenue is one cyclical segment, the group gross margin has fallen four years running, and H1 FY2026 delivered falling profit and an operating cash outflow on flat revenue. Bull cut to 25% because it needs three independent things -- offshore yard margin expansion, a liquid-food recovery and the newbuild ordering pace holding past the IMO delay -- to happen together. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a low-margin, capex-heavy Chinese clean-energy equipment maker with a net-cash balance sheet. The value is deliberately built from a 6.6% underlying EBITDA margin after stripping the RMB206m/yr the cash pile earns (which the market-facing 'other operating income' line hides) and after charging leases, SBC and the NCI exactly once; the net cash is then added at face. Terminal value is capped at 14x year-10 owner FCF -- a cyclical industrial, not a compounder. Risk is charged in the flows and the 25/50/25 weights, not by inflating the 8.5% CNY WACC. The headline is in HKD at the dated CNY->HKD rate so it is comparable to the quote.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: every 1pp of underlying EBITDA margin is roughly 15-20% of equity value at these conversion levels; the model assumes recovery to 7.3%, not to the 8% of FY2023-24
Capex normalisation: the FCF improvement rests on capex falling from 3.6% to 2.5% of revenue; a second shipyard or hydrogen capacity wave keeps it at 3.5% and removes most of the terminal FCF
Offshore order book cyclicality: RMB19.1bn backlog is scheduled through 2028; a newbuild-cycle rollover or Western restrictions on Chinese-built vessels hits FY2028-30 revenue directly
Working capital: shipbuilding and turnkey projects swing cash by RMB1-2bn/yr (FY2021 drain, FY2022 release, H1 FY2026 outflow); -5% capture is an average, not a forecast of any single year
Cash location: ~47% of the RMB7.6bn cash sits in partly-owned Safeway/CLPT; the book NCI deduction is a proxy for the minority's claim on it
FX: HKD value moves one-for-one with CNY/HKD; refresh_price.py updates the price but not fx_rate
Post-balance-date RMB1bn perpetual notes (equity-classified, 1.93%) are excluded; they rank ahead of common equity if ever treated as debt
